articles.title: Indian Restaurants Sweep UK's Nation's Curry Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: Aarti in Leeds took the overall Curry Restaurant of the Year title and Kolshi Premier in Warwick won Indian Restaurant of the Year at the 4th Nation's Curry Awards, celebrating the UK's vibrant curry industry.
articles.nri_angle: The awards spotlight the cultural and economic impact of the Indian diaspora on Britain's food industry, with family-run Indian restaurants winning top honours across every region of the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Chefs Are Taking Regional Cuisine Beyond Butter Chicken to Global Tables
articles.excerpt: From Michelin-starred South Indian restaurants in New York to Kerala cuisine in midtown Manhattan, a new generation of chefs and India's government are working to redefine the country's culinary identity abroad.
articles.image_caption: Indian chefs are bringing regional dishes beyond butter chicken to global fine dining tables, with restaurants like Semma earning Michelin stars.
articles.nri_angle: Directly about the global Indian food movement driven by diaspora chefs redefining Indian cuisine abroad
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Where to Find Chennai's Best Andhra Restaurants for Spicy Meals and Biryani
articles.excerpt: From no-frills mess halls to upscale regional dining rooms, Chennai's Andhra restaurant scene offers some of the city's most fiery and flavorful food — here's where to eat.
articles.nri_angle: Andhra cuisine in Chennai highlights India's vibrant regional food culture, a topic of deep interest for NRIs nostalgic for home-style meals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Simple Ways to Make Indian Food Healthier Without Giving Up Taste
articles.excerpt: Nutrition coaches say the solution is not abandoning Indian cuisine for Western diet trends — it is cooking smarter with the ingredients and traditions already in every Indian kitchen.
articles.image_caption: A balanced Indian meal with roti, dal, vegetables, and accompaniments arranged on a plate. Nutrition coaches say traditional Indian food already provides the right nutritional framework when cooked with moderation.
articles.nri_angle: Practical nutrition advice rooted in Indian cooking traditions, relevant to diaspora families balancing traditional meals with modern health awareness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mango Chia Pudding With Cardamom and Saffron: A Five-Minute Indian-Inspired Breakfast
articles.excerpt: This no-cook recipe combines ripe mango with cardamom, saffron, and pistachios — classic Indian dessert flavors in a wholesome make-ahead breakfast format.
articles.image_caption: Mango chia pudding topped with chopped pistachios and fresh mango in a glass jar. The Indian-inspired recipe combines cardamom and saffron with chia seeds for a no-cook breakfast or dessert.
articles.nri_angle: A familiar Indian flavor combination — mango, cardamom, saffron, pistachios — reimagined as a convenient make-ahead breakfast for diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bhajiya: How to Make the Perfect Assorted Indian Fritters at Home
articles.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to making crisp, golden mixed bhajiya — the classic Indian street snack of batter-fried potato, brinjal, chilli, and bread.
articles.image_caption: A platter of assorted bhajiya including potato, brinjal, chilli, and bread fritters served with green chutney. The crisp gram flour-coated fritters are a staple street food across Gujarat and Maharashtra.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian diaspora families craving monsoon-season comfort food, bhajiya with chai is the ultimate taste of home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ITC's Dakshin Crowned India's Best South Indian Restaurant at National Awards
articles.excerpt: The iconic Mumbai restaurant beat five other nominees at the Zee Zest Unlimit Awards 2026, as Kerala and South Indian cuisine enjoy a global moment.
articles.nri_angle: Kerala and South Indian cuisine are gaining unprecedented global recognition, with diaspora restaurants in New York and Leeds earning top honors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Moves to Ban Fake Paneer as States Crack Down on Dairy Fraud
articles.excerpt: FSSAI plans to outright prohibit analogue paneer while Maharashtra has already imposed a one-year state-wide ban, with 35% of tested samples failing safety standards.
articles.nri_angle: Affects the quality of paneer available across India, a staple food for the Indian diaspora visiting or sending for family back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Domino's and Five Other Eatery Licences Over Food Safety Violations
articles.excerpt: A statewide enforcement drive found cockroach infestations, expired ingredients, and missing safety documentation across six food establishments in Maharashtra.
articles.image_caption: A food inspector examines a restaurant kitchen. Maharashtra's FDA has suspended licences of six eateries including major fast food chains over serious food safety violations.
articles.nri_angle: The crackdown on major food chains raises awareness for Indian Americans who frequent these brands during visits to India and highlights the growing push for food safety enforcement in the country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Family-Run Indian Restaurant Near Newark Wins National Best Restaurant Award
articles.excerpt: The Ashiana in North Muskham takes home Best Restaurant of the Year at the Curry Life Awards, adding to a growing list of East Midlands honours.
articles.nri_angle: The Ashiana reflects the enduring legacy of Bangladeshi families in Britain's curry industry, representing a model of diaspora entrepreneurship built on traditional flavours and personalised service.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From School Dropout to IPO: How Sathish Kumar Built the Rs 10,000 Crore Milky Mist Dairy Empire
articles.excerpt: The Erode teenager who taught himself to make paneer is now taking his dairy company public with a Rs 1,553 crore offering
articles.nri_angle: Milky Mist's IPO and national expansion highlight how a small-town Indian dairy brand built on paneer — a staple in diaspora kitchens worldwide — is entering public markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How a Bengaluru Startup Turns Fruit Waste Into Ingredients That Replace Microplastics
articles.excerpt: BacAlt Biosciences ferments agricultural waste into biopolymers that can replace the synthetic additives found in shampoos, toothpaste, and cleaning products.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian startup addressing the global microplastics problem through biotechnology, with implications for India's speciality ingredients industry and export ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Trader Joe's $2.99 Frozen Garlic Naan Has Become a Cult Favorite
articles.excerpt: At four pieces for under three dollars, the frozen flatbread has earned praise from Indian food lovers and budget shoppers alike — and it outranks most of the store's other Indian offerings.
articles.image_caption: Trader Joe's frozen garlic naan, sold in packs of four for $2.99. The product has earned a devoted following among Indian food fans and budget-conscious shoppers.
articles.nri_angle: A convenient, affordable version of a staple Indian bread that diaspora families keep stocked for quick meals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sawan Fasting? This No-Onion, No-Garlic Paneer Sabji Is Ready in 20 Minutes
articles.excerpt: A rich, creamy paneer curry that follows sattvic cooking principles for Shravan fasting — using whole spices, tomatoes, and cashew paste instead of the usual onion-garlic base.
articles.image_caption: A traditional paneer dish, a staple of Indian vegetarian cooking. The no-onion, no-garlic paneer sabji is popular during the Sawan fasting period observed by Hindus.
articles.nri_angle: Shravan fasting is widely observed by Hindu diaspora families, who often struggle to find sattvic recipes that are both authentic and practical for weeknight cooking abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How a Bengaluru Couple's Homesickness Built India's Hottest Dosa Brand
articles.excerpt: Akhil Iyer and Shriya Narayan turned a craving for Davangere-style benne dosa into a Rs 350 crore brand with three Mumbai outlets, a Delhi presence, and billionaire investor interest.
articles.image_caption: Benne, the fast-growing dosa chain founded by Bengaluru couple Akhil Iyer and Shriya Narayan. The brand has expanded from a single 275-square-foot Bandra outlet to multiple cities, with a valuation of Rs 350 crore.
articles.nri_angle: Benne dosa is a Bengaluru staple now expanding nationally, part of a broader wave of regional Indian food brands gaining mainstream attention and investor interest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Coastal Karnataka's Ancient Food-as-Medicine Tradition Is Vanishing, Workshop Warns
articles.excerpt: At a workshop near Mangalore, scholars and food creators say traditional dishes calibrated to seasonal health needs are being lost to steel vessels and gas stoves.
articles.image_caption: Speakers at the Disappearing Tulunadu Food Culture workshop at the Rani Abbakka Tulu Museum in B.C. Road near Mangalore. The event highlighted the erosion of traditional cooking methods in coastal Karnataka.
articles.nri_angle: The disappearing food traditions of Tulu Nadu resonate with the large Mangalorean diaspora's cultural connection to their homeland cuisine.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doodhi Halwa: How to Make the Classic Bottle Gourd Dessert Without Khoya
articles.excerpt: This simplified Punjabi recipe turns a humble lauki into a rich, cardamom-scented halwa in under 45 minutes — no specialty ingredients required.
articles.image_caption: A serving of doodhi halwa garnished with chopped nuts and saffron strands. The traditional Punjabi dessert is made from grated bottle gourd slow-cooked with milk, sugar, and cardamom.
articles.nri_angle: Bottle gourd is increasingly available at Indian grocery stores and mainstream supermarkets in the US, UK, and Canada, making doodhi halwa an accessible traditional dessert for diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Story of South Indian Filter Coffee: From Smuggled Beans to a Global Morning Ritual
articles.excerpt: How seven coffee beans smuggled from Yemen in the 17th century gave rise to India's most beloved brewing tradition and a cultural identity that travels with the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: A traditional South Indian steel coffee filter used to brew decoction by slow drip. The two-chambered device has been the heart of filter kaapi culture across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka for over a century.
articles.nri_angle: Filter kaapi has followed the South Indian diaspora worldwide, with the steel filter and tumbler-dabara remaining essential items in NRI kitchens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Simple Tests to Check If Your Paneer Is Real or Fake at Home
articles.excerpt: As India cracks down on synthetic dairy products, FSSAI-backed tests using iodine, warm water, and a hot pan can help consumers identify adulterated paneer before it reaches their plate.
articles.nri_angle: Paneer quality and food safety is a universal concern for Indian households worldwide, particularly for diaspora families who rely on it as a primary protein source and often purchase from specialty stores where provenance is harder to verify
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kanwar Yatra Camps Blend Tradition and Street Food With 7,000 Rotis a Day
articles.excerpt: Volunteer camps along the Uttar Pradesh pilgrimage route serve everything from shahi paneer and dal makhani to pizza, momos, and pasta — all prepared without onion and garlic.
articles.image_caption: Kanwar Yatris carry holy water from the Ganges during the annual pilgrimage. Food camps along the route serve thousands of rotis and traditional street food daily.
articles.nri_angle: The Kanwar Yatra is one of India's most iconic religious pilgrimages, and its evolving food culture reflects the broader fusion of tradition and modernity that resonates with the diaspora
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Bars Crack Asia's 50 Best List as Goa's Boilermaker Storms Into Top 10
articles.excerpt: Boilermaker in Goa jumped 22 places to No. 8, while Bengaluru's SOKA and Bar Spirit Forward reinforced the city's growing reputation as India's cocktail capital.
articles.image_caption: The interior of Boilermaker in Siolim, Goa. The bar jumped 22 places to No. 8 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 and was named Best Bar in India.
articles.nri_angle: India's growing presence on the global cocktail stage is a point of pride for NRIs, many of whom visit these bars when traveling home and follow the country's evolving food and drink scene.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nick and Joe Jonas Snack on Bhajia, Kachori, and Papad During Tour Break
articles.excerpt: The Jonas Brothers continue to embrace Indian cuisine on their 20th anniversary tour, with Nick's love for Indian food now a recurring highlight of their social media presence.
articles.nri_angle: Nick Jonas's genuine embrace of Indian food and Bollywood culture has made him a beloved figure among the Indian diaspora, turning casual snack moments into cultural touchpoints.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Himachali Siddu: How To Make the Mountain Bread That Fueled Himalayan Shepherds
articles.excerpt: This steamed, walnut-stuffed bread from Himachal Pradesh is centuries old, protein-rich, and easy to make at home with just wheat flour, yeast, and a handful of nuts and herbs.
articles.image_caption: Siddu, a traditional steamed bread from Himachal Pradesh, is made with wheat dough stuffed with a spiced filling and cooked over a slow flame.
articles.nri_angle: Siddu uses pantry staples available worldwide, making it an accessible way for diaspora families to connect with Himachali mountain food traditions at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: What Made Your Thali Costlier in July: Onions, Oil, and Chicken Drive Kitchen Inflation
articles.excerpt: Home-cooked vegetarian meals rose 4% and non-vegetarian meals 9% year-on-year as onion, oil, LPG, and chicken prices surged, a Crisil report finds.
articles.nri_angle: The thali cost index is a useful barometer of food inflation for diaspora families tracking the cost of living back home in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FSSAI Penalises Fortune Oil Maker AWL After Sunflower Oil Fails Vitamin D Test
articles.excerpt: India's food safety regulator has taken action against AWL Agri Business, formerly Adani Wilmar, after a Fortune sunflower oil sample did not meet mandatory Vitamin D fortification standards, part of an intensifying crackdown on food labelling and quality.
articles.nri_angle: Fortune is widely available in Indian grocery stores across the US, UK and Canada; diaspora consumers buying imported Fortune oil should check fortification labels.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Zorawar Kalra Built a Global Indian Restaurant Empire From His Father's Legacy
articles.excerpt: The son of legendary food critic Jiggs Kalra reveals how he recruited two of India's best young chefs to launch Masala Library — and turned Indian food into a global brand with 50 restaurants and counting.
articles.image_caption: The late Jiggs Kalra, known as the Czar of Indian cuisine, whose culinary legacy his son Zorawar has expanded into a global restaurant empire.
articles.nri_angle: Kalra's plan to open 50 restaurants across North America directly targets the Indian diaspora market, filling a gap in casual modern Indian dining that cities like New York, Toronto, and the Bay Area currently lack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sweetgreen Cuts Full-Year Outlook as Cyclospora Outbreak Tanks Salad Demand
articles.excerpt: The salad chain slashed its same-store sales forecast and warned of prolonged consumer hesitancy toward fresh produce, even though none of its ingredients have been linked to the nationwide illness.
articles.image_caption: Sweetgreen shares have fallen roughly 30% over the past month as the nationwide cyclospora outbreak reduced consumer demand for salads and fresh produce. The chain cut its full-year same-store sales forecast nearly in half on Thursday.
articles.nri_angle: The cyclospora outbreak affects Indian-American consumers who frequent salad chains, while raising parallels with food safety standards in the broader restaurant industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kolkata's Iconic Flurys Opens First North India Outlet in Gurugram Ahead of Centenary
articles.excerpt: The 99-year-old tearoom brings its Park Street heritage to Galleria Market as it eyes a national footprint before its 2027 centenary.
articles.image_caption: Flurys, the iconic Kolkata tearoom on Park Street, has opened its first outlet in North India at Gurugram's Galleria Market ahead of its centenary in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: For Bengalis and Kolkata natives abroad, Flurys evokes deep nostalgia — its expansion signals that iconic local brands are scaling nationally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Today Investigation Exposes Sprawling Fake Dairy Racket Across Delhi-NCR
articles.excerpt: Undercover reporting reveals synthetic paneer, adulterated milk, and fake khoya flowing into restaurants and street vendors, raising alarm about food safety enforcement gaps.
articles.nri_angle: The investigation highlights food safety risks that concern diaspora members who regularly consume dairy products during visits to India and worry about the authenticity of Indian dairy exports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
